newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say regional lifting of UK beef ban possible.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say regional lifting of UK beef ban possible.

text.p: Beef from proven BSE-free herds in some areas of Britain should be exempt from a worldwide export ban on British beef, Dutch Agriculture Minister Jozias van Aartsen said on Wednesday.

The European Union imposed the global ban in March to protect public health after the British government admitted that the disease, known as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could be transmitted to humans who ate infected beef.

"There are possibilities...in some regions in Northern Ireland and Scotland, where there has never been a problem with the disease, where you can identify BSE-free farms, and you should give them the opportunity to export," Van Aartsen told a news briefing.
The Netherlands assumes the six-month rotating presidency of the EU in January and Van Aartsen said the BSE problem was likely to out-live the Dutch term.
"The export ban as it stands now can't be lifted for months." he said.
On Tuesday, Britain submitted a proposal to the European Commission for exempting grass-fed herds that are free of so-called mad cow disease from the worldwide ban.
Northern Irish farmers in particular have campaigned hard for exemption from the crippling ban, pointing to a computerised system for identifying and tracing animals from birth.
Britain last month shelved the start-up of a programme imposed by the EU to slaughter up to 147,000 extra cattle at risk to the fatal brain-wasting disease.
The cull was in addition to the slaughter of animals aged over 30 months and destruction of the carcasses to prevent them entering the food chain.
Britain has so far killed almost 600,000 such animals, but there is a backlog of 400,000 animals awaiting slaughter.
